findings.issue: The renderer-output-fingerprint exclusion test does not exercise the production input-assembly path and cannot detect verbosity entering the output fingerprint. It re-implements the RenderFingerprintInput construction in a local helper whose only snapshot-derived fields are RendererConfigurationFingerprint (already proven equal by the preceding test) and RendererOutputPolicy (code-owned default). The two inputs are therefore identical by construction, so the output/request fingerprint equality is a pure determinism assertion on equal inputs, not an independent verbosity-exclusion test. A regression that threaded snapshot.LogVerbosity into RenderFingerprintInput (e.g. a new field with a default) would leave this test green, because the helper never supplies verbosity. The production path assembles the input from request.ConfigurationFingerprint / BadgeDefinitions / RendererOutputPolicy in ArtworkRegenerationPlanner.ComputeDesiredFingerprint and SkiaBadgeRenderer, none of which the test touches.

findings.recommended_action: Drive the real path with two snapshots differing only in LogVerbosity (e.g. ArtworkRegenerationPlanner.ComputeDesiredFingerprint or Decide with the published-state fixture) and assert the desired/published fingerprint is identical and the decision is Skip; that single test would cover output-fingerprint exclusion, RenderVersion, and 'never republishes artwork' on the production path.

findings.issue: The RenderVersion assertions restate a compile-time constant. RenderVersion.CurrentRendererVersion is a const int, and the test-built inputs never pass a rendererVersion argument, so 'input.RendererVersion == RenderVersion.CurrentRendererVersion' cannot vary with verbosity or anything else. The assertion adds no evidence for the 'never changes RenderVersion' claim.
findings.recommended_action: Replace with a behavioral assertion (a verbosity-only snapshot replacement yields the same planner desired fingerprint / a Skip decision) or drop the tautological assertion and rely on the structural const guarantee.

findings.issue: HostLoggingResolvesWithArrTagsCategoryPrefixes largely restates framework and namespace behavior. ILogger<Plugin> resolves with category typeof(Plugin).FullName by Microsoft.Extensions.Logging convention, and the 'ArrTags.' prefix is a property of the Plugin type's namespace rather than anything ArrTags configures (this task adds no log call site). The test does prove the host provider is reachable through the container after registration, but the category assertions are near-tautological.
evidence: src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:44-48 registers only ILogVerbosityGate and no logging services
findings.recommended_action: Keep as boundary documentation; when task 10.2 adds call sites, assert the actual emitted categories/SourceContext rather than the type-name convention.

findings.issue: 'Changing verbosity never republishes artwork' (ADR-020 clause 5, docs/architecture.md:303) is established only transitively: no test replaces the snapshot with a verbosity-only change through the regeneration planner or publishing pipeline. It follows logically from the proven fingerprint equality plus the existing fingerprint-gated Skip in ArtworkRegenerationPlanner, and the task's stated test list did not require an end-to-end republish test.

summary: The task's core claims are established. Fingerprint exclusion is non-vacuously proven on the real configuration-fingerprint path (two snapshots differing only in LogVerbosity produce the same RendererConfigurationFingerprint), and there is no code path by which verbosity enters an output fingerprint or changes RenderVersion (structural verification: LogVerbosity is absent from the Rendering/artwork fingerprint code and RenderVersion is a const). Bounded enum validation with a secret-free message, last-valid-snapshot retention, all six gating levels including Off, apply-without-restart through the registrator-resolved gate, the settings-page control, the legacy-XML Warning default, and the no-custom-ILoggerProvider/no-host-ILoggerFactory-replacement check are all genuinely tested and non-vacuous. Skips are honest and unchanged at 63; the suite is deterministic across repeated runs (1298/63/1361). The single material test-quality gap is TQ-10.1-01 (MEDIUM): the test named for renderer-output-fingerprint exclusion re-implements the RenderFingerprintInput assembly and would not fail if verbosity were added directly to the output fingerprint; its RenderVersion assertions are tautological (TQ-10.1-02). No BLOCKER or HIGH finding and no must-fix item: the documented matrix accurately reflects what the suite establishes, so the verdict is CONCERNS with recommended (non-blocking) test strengthening rather than a clean PASS.
